terms.gloss: a market of eating-houses: a food court
terms.comment: A description of ours: no reference work searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for a food court. It is made as Rome named its markets by what was sold there, Forum Bovārium, Forum Holitōrium, Forum Piscārium, as Varro explains (LL 5.146), with popīna, an eating-house (see “restaurant”). Rome’s forum cuppēdinis was a market for delicacies, not a place to eat.

phrases.latin: In forō popīnārum prandeāmus: ibi suum quisque cibum ēliget.
phrases.english: Let’s have lunch in the food court: there everyone can choose his own food.

phrases.latin: Ubi quid generātim, additum ab eō cognōmen, ut Forum Bovārium, Forum Holitōrium.
phrases.english: Where something is sold by kind, a name was added from it, as the Cattle Market and the Vegetable Market.

sources: Lewis & Short: popina · Lewis & Short: forum
